correctness.rationale: Under \(f_\eta\), the disjoint unique semicircle-anchor events have density \(nf_\eta(\theta)p_\eta(\theta)^{n-1}\), with \(p_\eta=(1-b\sin\theta)/2\). Integrating a full-period derivative cancels the cosine-weight contribution and gives the exact finite polynomial. The far endpoint has explicit conditional order-statistic survival \((1-q_\eta/p_\eta)^{n-1}\); Laplace expansion around the unique maximum at \(-\pi/2\) proves the fixed-anisotropy Gaussian scale and probability coefficient. First-order endpoint mass gives the exponential scale, jointly; for \(\eta_n=\lambda/n\), bounded convergence yields the normalized von Mises law and uniform endpoint exponential. Pointwise normalized joint densities imply total variation by Scheffé. The diameter-disk theorem exactly relates these variables to the minimum enclosing center and radius. Reproducible finite computations corroborated these steps, but are not infinite proofs.

value.rationale: A smallest enclosing disk is a canonical geometric stability descriptor. Conditioning on radius below the ambient-circle radius is exponentially rare, and the conditional center has a nontrivial symmetry-breaking transition exactly when the first Fourier bias has size 1/n. The result explicitly determines the rare-event rate, the circular von Mises crossover, the Gaussian localization scale, and the independent exponential radial mark; it is not a change of notation or a routine finite count.
